requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

The sheet identifies D01 as deep indigo denim, 340 g/m², 1450 mm wide, with two 4000 mm rolls, and D02 as faded blue denim, 270 g/m², 1350 mm wide, with one 3000 mm roll. Both are recorded as prewashed right-hand twill, 98% cotton and 2% elastane. It maps P01/F01, P02/F02 and P03/F03, states each costume's chosen finished hip and knee circumferences, specifies a 10 mm seam allowance, and gives usable seam and closure specifications. Seam and closure choices may vary; missing fields or inventory contradictions fail.

Specified construction uses the supplied stock and compatible supplies: indigo polyester Tex 40 sewing thread, pale-blue polyester Tex 60 topstitching thread, up to three indigo closed-end 200 mm coil zips, up to eighteen complete matte-black 12 mm press-stud sets, up to 3000 mm of black 30 mm elastic, and opaque-white printing ink. Any stated consumption must remain within the recorded quantities, including 2000 m sewing thread, 1000 m topstitching thread and 100 ml ink. Using only a subset is allowed; specifying unavailable substitutes or exceeding available quantities fails.

The materials sheet, each cutting sheet and the presentation explicitly state both fabric IDs, all three costume IDs and the 10 mm seam allowance. Each enlarged detail explicitly states D01, D02 and the same allowance. A clear range notation for the three costume IDs is acceptable; omission, substitution or a conflicting allowance fails.

Dimensioned, identified cutting outlines and quantities account for all six garments and three self-fabric patches. D01-A and D01-B remain separate layouts, each inside a 1400 × 3900 mm usable rectangle; D02-A uses 1300 × 2900 mm. These areas respect the 25 mm long-edge and 50 mm end exclusions within the full rolls. Allocated pieces do not overlap or cross usable boundaries, and grain arrows keep warp parallel to roll length. Area calculations use cutting outlines including seam allowances. Each roll's allocated and remaining areas reconcile to 5.460, 5.460 or 3.770 m² respectively, totaling 14.690 m². Different valid nesting arrangements are allowed; omitted quantities, pooled D01 rolls, impossible placement or inconsistent arithmetic fail.

Both summary documents state chosen hip/knee circumferences meeting F01 ≥1060/450 mm, F02 ≥1160/480 mm and F03 ≥1280/520 mm. Corresponding cutting-sheet seam-line dimensions, assembled using the indicated quantities, support those same finished values without counting seam allowances as ease. Larger circumferences are allowed. Values below a minimum, mismatched costume assignments, missing seam-line dimensions or contradictory assembled totals fail.

The front sheet shows front flats of three tops and three trousers; the back sheet shows their back flats. Every garment is attributable to F01, F02 or F03, and panels are labeled with their applicable fabric ID. Patch dimensions are provided where the left-chest patches are depicted on the front sheet. Layout and silhouette choices are free; missing garments, wrong view orientation or ambiguous costume/fabric labeling fail.

Each role shows its assigned performer standing in the corresponding complete costume: P01/F01, P02/F02 or P03/F03. Both top and trousers can be inspected together. Pose and framing may vary while preserving this evidence; a missing garment, incorrect assignment or framing that prevents inspection fails.

Each costume remains identifiable across its flats, standing view and both ensemble poses through compatible silhouettes, fabric-panel boundaries and closure locations. Front and back information describes one constructible garment pair per costume. Drape, foreshortening and pose-related occlusion are allowed; changing garment identity, fabric allocation or closure placement fails.

The reach sheet shows all three assigned costumes with both arms extended overhead, separated hands and grounded feet. The squat sheet shows all three with hips below knees, grounded heels and arms forward. Costume IDs and relevant underarm, hip and knee construction remain inspectable. Panel IDs on both enlarged junctions link unambiguously to the depicted garments. Natural deformation is allowed; missing performers, incorrect poses or unmatched junction identifiers fail.

The underarm detail resolves the underarm panel connection, and the crotch detail resolves the crotch and inner-leg connection. Each shows applicable fabric IDs, a 10 mm seam allowance and readable stitch paths consistent with the craft specification. Panel identifiers locate the corresponding cutting pieces. Drawing style and seam method may vary; generic unlinked close-ups, missing stitch information or incompatible piece connections fail.

Every depicted top has one patch on the wearer's left chest. The front flats dimension the finished patch as 80 × 25 mm, and standing views show a consistent size and placement. Each patch legibly places FOLDLINE on the first line and Move together below it. Typography may vary; reversed placement, incorrect line order, missing patches or unreadable required wording fail.

The opening page visibly includes the exact collection name FOLDLINE and phrase Move together. Their page layout is unrestricted; wording appearing only on later pages, omission or altered spelling fails.

Each complete costume visibly uses both deep indigo and faded blue denim, with its fabric allocation consistent between labels and worn appearance. The distribution between top and trousers is open. A costume using only one stock fabric, swapped fabric identities or an unexplained additional garment fabric fails; numeric ease is assessed from the measurement records.
From the audience viewpoint, the three assigned performers appear in P01, P02, P03 order. Perspective may vary while keeping this order verifiable; reversed or exchanged positions fail.

Adjacent performer centres are depicted consistently with 1200 mm spacing, using any supplied scale cues or annotations and allowing perspective compression. An exact pixel separation is not required. Clearly conflicting dimensions or substantially unequal physical spacing fail.
All three performers occupy a single straight formation on the stage plane. Perspective projection is allowed; a triangular, curved or staggered-depth formation fails.

Review the full 12-second timeline: 0–3 seconds shows neutral upright standing with arms beside the body and feet shoulder-width apart; 3–6 shows both arms overhead with hands separated and feet grounded; 6–9 shows hips below knees, heels grounded and arms forward; 9–12 shows staggered rising initiated by P01 at 9 seconds, P02 at 10 and P03 at 11, with everyone standing at 12. The audience order is P01/P02/P03 in one straight line with 1200 mm centre spacing. The same assigned tops, trousers, fabric boundaries and closures persist from the source images. Natural continuous transitions are allowed; incorrect phase timing, simultaneous rise starts, missing performers or costume changes fail.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation visibly incorporates recognizable material from the earlier sheets and views, plus stills traceable to the delivered video. Cropping, scaling and combining several items on a page are allowed when source identity and relevant information remain recognizable. A written mention without visible reuse, unrelated replacement artwork or a missing source fails.

The presentation contains exactly ten pages and ends with an individually identified balance for D01-A, D01-B and D02-A. The closing figures agree with the cutting sheets and reconcile allocated plus remaining usable stock for each roll. Presented costume specifications and depictions preserve the developed six-garment collection. Page composition is free; an incorrect page count, an absent roll, contradictory totals or changed costume specifications fail.

The three costumes establish a discernible relationship of pale and dark panel placement, and that relationship remains recognizable across standing, reaching and squatting. Identical panel arrangements are not required, and folds may partially obscure panels. Unrelated costume arrangements or movement depictions that replace the established light-dark pattern fail.

F01, F02 and F03 retain compatible garment silhouettes, D01/D02 panel boundaries and closure locations across the collection. Enlarged junctions match the garments and the cutting-piece identifiers, seam allowances and construction specifications. Each complete costume uses both stock fabrics and remains assigned to its specified performer.

The relationship between pale and dark panels remains recognizable across the three costumes and changing body positions. The movement sheets preserve the specified performer order, straight-line formation and centre spacing.
